q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS V1 GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS V1 GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 201, '2023-01-02');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE. This difference in grouping affects the results when the same VIEWER_ID has multiple VIEW_DATEs with the same ARTICLE_IDs.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have a VIEWER_ID that has the same ARTICLE_ID on different VIEW_DATEs. Q1 will not count this as it groups by VIEW_DATE first, while Q2 will count it as it groups by VIEWER_ID first.
